review.summary: changes_needed. Checks run: check_links bad 0; pytest 108 passed (includes the contents-list invariant; make_toc --check itself was blocked by permissions; no network, so external sources were checked from memory only). Top findings: (1) Week 7 recap says every component "is ablated, and removed, when the model improves", contradicting 7.6's world-limit rule. (2) 7.6 answer cites "the lying tool" with no link or explanation; it is Week 2.5's lying bash. (3) Several terms appear in Week 7 before being explained (LangSmith/OpenEvals, xhigh effort, p90, Puppeteer MCP, Playwright).

findings.checklist_item: Plain language: simplifying must not change meaning; review recap must not strengthen a claim beyond the lesson body
findings.title: Week 7 recap says components are removed when the model improves; 7.6 says world-limit components stay
findings.claim: The recap of 7.6 ends: "Every component is an assumption about what the model cannot do. It is ablated, and removed, when the model improves." The lesson body says the opposite for world-limit components: the provenance guard is "never retire[d]", the weather script is kept "whatever happens", and the diagram's model-limit branch ends in "Still needed? yes → Keep it, record why". The lesson's own "Typical slips" names "calling every component model-limit" as the error; the recap commits it.
findings.evidence: Line 952 vs. lines 866–881 ("*World-limit*, so never retire it"; "Keep the script whatever happens") and diagrams/src/component-assumption.mmd lines 3 and 8 ("Keep it, whatever the model"; "Keep it, record why").
findings.proposed_change: Reword the recap sentence to match the body, e.g.: "Every component is an assumption about what the model cannot do. Re-test it with a removal ablation when the model changes, and remove it only if it guarded a model limit that is gone; components that guard the world (outages, forged documents) stay."

findings.checklist_item: Visuals: does the diagram match the text? wrong arrows
findings.title: Chained arrows between sibling options imply a data flow the text does not describe
findings.claim: The four online layers are drawn L1 → L2 → L3 → L4 with solid arrows, which reads as 'deterministic signals feed the judges, which feed delayed ground truth'. The text presents them as independent layers ordered by cost, all feeding the annotation queue (which the `L1 & L2 & L3 --> Q` edge also encodes, so every layer now has two outgoing arrows). world-stand-ins.mmd lines 4–7 do the same for the four world options (W1 → W2 → W3 → W4), where the only relation is an ordering by realism.
findings.evidence: diagrams/src/online-eval-layers.mmd lines 2–6; diagrams/src/world-stand-ins.mmd lines 4–7; lesson text lines 517–537 ("Think of it as four layers, cheapest first").
findings.proposed_change: Use dotted edges (`-.->`) or a `subgraph` with no inter-layer edges for the ordering, and keep only the layer → queue arrows solid. Re-render with python3 tools/render_diagrams.py online-eval-layers world-stand-ins and check at phone width.
